```{r}
library(spls)
library(MHPCA)
data("yeast")

# ChIP-chip data
x <- yeast$x
colnames(x) <- sub("_YPD$", "", colnames(x))
# gene expression functional 542 genes and and each column is mrna level measure at each 7 minutes
y <- yeast$y
rm(yeast)


# Create B-spline basis and multivariate functional data (mfd) objects
v1 <- t(y)
scaling_factor_tfunction <- sqrt(mean(diag(var(v1))))
v1 <- 1/sqrt(mean(diag(var(v1))))*v1
nbasis_f <- 16
t0_f <- 0
t1_f <- 119
grid_point <- ncol(y)
t <- seq(t0_f, t1_f, length.out = grid_point)
bspline_basis <- fda::create.bspline.basis(c(t0_f,t1_f),nbasis_f)
mfd_basis <- basismfd$new(bspline_basis)
mfd_v1 <- mfd$new(t,v1,mfd_basis)
hd_obj1f <- Hd(list(mfd_v1))

#vector data
vector_data <- x
scaling_factor_vector <- sqrt(mean(diag(var(vector_data))))
vector_data <- 1/scaling_factor_vector*vector_data
nfd_obj1 <- nfd(vector_data)

hd_obj <- Hd(mfd_v1,nfd_obj1)
```

```{r}
# Load required libraries

plot_expression_virdis <- function(y) {
  # Load required libraries
  require(ggplot2)
  require(reshape2)
  require(viridis)
  df <- melt(y)
  names(df) <- c("Series", "Time", "Expression")
  df$Time <- as.numeric(sub("alpha", "", df$Time))
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Time, y = Expression, group = Series, color = factor(Series))) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 119, by = 7),expand = expansion(.01)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-3, 5), breaks = seq(-3, 5, by = 1)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 60, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
    scale_color_viridis_d(option = "H") +
    labs(x = "Time (minutes)", y = "Expression level") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  return(p)
}
plot_expression_virdis(y)

```

plot_fpc <- function(mat, fpc = 1, main = "My Plot", xlab = "X-axis", ylab = "Y-axis") {
  # Determine the column name and y-range (with na.rm in case of missing values)
  colname <- paste0("fpc", fpc)
  y_range <- range(mat, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Save current graphical parameters and set new ones for publication quality
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  par(cex.axis = 1.2,   # Increase axis tick label size
      cex.lab  = 1.3,   # Increase axis label size
      cex.main = 1.5,   # Increase title size
      mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2) + 0.1)  # Adjust margins
  
  # Create the plot with enhanced line width and without default axes (we'll add them manually)
  plot(mat[, fpc], type = "l", main = main, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab,
       ylim = y_range, lwd = 2, col = "black", axes = FALSE)
  
  # Draw custom axes and a surrounding box
  axis(1, cex.axis = 1.2)
  axis(2, cex.axis = 1.2)
  box()
  
  # Add a grey horizontal line at y = 0
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey", lwd = 2)
  
  # Add a grey dashed vertical line at x = 60
  abline(v = 60, col = "grey", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  
  # Restore original graphical parameters
  par(old_par)
}

plot_fpc_pn <- function(data, fpc = 1, main = "My Plot", xlab = "X-axis", ylab = "Y-axis") {
  p_col <- paste0("p", fpc)
  n_col <- paste0("n", fpc)
  y_range <- range(data$f_mean, data[[p_col]], data[[n_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  plot(data$f_mean, type = "l", main = main, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, ylim = c(-.05,.2))
  points(data[[p_col]], col = "blue", pch = "+")
  points(data[[n_col]], col = "red", pch = "-")

  #        col = c("black", "blue", "red"),

}

```{r}
library(reshape2)
plot_fpc_gg <- function(t0_f, t1_f, res, hd_obj,
                          fpc_index = 1, alpha = 0.1,
                          main = "My Plot", xlab = "Time (minutes)", ylab = "Expression Level",y_limits = c(-.25,.25)) {
  # Generate a time grid
  tt <- seq(t0_f, t1_f, length.out = 119)
  
  # Evaluate principal component loadings at time grid
  pc_loadings <- res$pc_hd$eval(tt)
  fpc <- pc_loadings[[1]]
  colnames(fpc) <- paste0("fpc", 1:ncol(fpc))
  
  nfpc <- t(pc_loadings[[2]])
  colnames(nfpc) <- paste0("nfpc", 1:ncol(nfpc))
  
  # Evaluate the mean function
  ave <- res$mean_hd$eval(tt)
  f_ave <- ave[[1]]
  colnames(f_ave) <- "f_mean"
  
  nf_ave <- t(ave[[2]])
  colnames(nf_ave) <- "nf_mean"
  
  # Compute positive and negative perturbations from the mean
  fpc_positive <- as.vector(f_ave) + alpha * fpc 
  fpc_negative <- as.vector(f_ave) - alpha * fpc 
  colnames(fpc_positive) <- paste0("p", 1:ncol(fpc_positive))
  colnames(fpc_negative) <- paste0("n", 1:ncol(fpc_negative))
  
  # Combine into a single data frame and add time
  fpc_df <- cbind(f_ave, fpc_positive, fpc_negative) |> as.data.frame()
  fpc_df$time <- tt
  
  # Select the columns corresponding to the specified fpc index
  p_col <- paste0("p", fpc_index)
  n_col <- paste0("n", fpc_index)
  
  # Reshape the data to long format for ggplot2
  
  df_long <- melt(fpc_df, id.vars = "time", 
                  measure.vars = c("f_mean", p_col, n_col),
                  variable.name = "variable", 
                  value.name = "value")
  
  # Define custom colors for each series
  my_colors <- c("f_mean" = "black")
  my_colors[p_col] <- "blue"
  my_colors[n_col] <- "red"
  
  p <- ggplot(df_long, aes(x = time, y = value, group = variable, color = factor(variable))) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.7,size = 1.2) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 119, by = 7)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(y_limits[1], y_limits[2]), breaks = seq(y_limits[1], y_limits[2], by = .05)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 60, linetype = "dashed", color = "green", size = .5) +
    scale_color_manual(name = "",values = my_colors,labels = c("Mean", "Positive", "Negative")) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  return(p)
}
plot_fpc_gg(t0_f = 0,t1_f = 119,res = res_power_sparse,hd_obj = hd_obj,fpc_index = 1,alpha = .3)
plot_fpc_gg(t0_f = 0,t1_f = 119,res = res_power_sparse,hd_obj = hd_obj,fpc_index = 2,alpha = .3)
plot_fpc_gg(t0_f = 0,t1_f = 119,res = res_power_sparse,hd_obj = hd_obj,fpc_index = 3,alpha = .3)
plot_fpc_gg(t0_f = 0,t1_f = 119,res = res_power_sparse,hd_obj = hd_obj,fpc_index = 4,alpha = .3)
```

# plot fpc's in one plot
```{r}
plot_fpc_vecs <- function(vecs, 
                          main = "My Plot", 
                          xlab = "X-axis", 
                          ylab = "Y-axis", 
                          legend_title = "Series",
                          vline_x = 60,
                          x_breaks = NULL, 
                          y_limits = NULL, 
                          y_break_by = 0.05,
                          colors = NULL, 
                          alpha = 0.7, 
                          size = 1.2) {
  # If the list of vectors does not have names, assign default names
  if (is.null(names(vecs))) {
    names(vecs) <- paste0("Series", seq_along(vecs))
  }
  
  # Create a data frame for each vector with its x-values (using sequence along the vector)
  df_list <- lapply(names(vecs), function(nm) {
    v <- vecs[[nm]]
    data.frame(Time = seq_along(v),
               Expression = v,
               Series = nm)
  })
  
  # Combine into one data frame
  df <- do.call(rbind, df_list)
  
  # Determine global x-axis range
  x_range <- range(sapply(vecs, length))
  if (is.null(x_breaks)) {
    x_breaks <- seq(x_range[1], x_range[2], by = 7)
  }
  
  # Determine global y-axis limits from all vectors if not supplied
  if (is.null(y_limits)) {
    y_limits <- range(df$Expression, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  y_breaks <- seq(y_limits[1], y_limits[2], by = y_break_by)
  
  # Build the plot
  library(ggplot2)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Time, y = Expression, group = Series, color = factor(Series))) +
    geom_line(alpha = alpha, size = size) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 119, by = 7)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = y_limits, breaks = y_breaks) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = vline_x, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
    labs(title = main, x = xlab, y = ylab, color = legend_title) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
  
  # If user-supplied colors are provided, use them; otherwise use a default viridis scale
  if (!is.null(colors)) {
    p <- p + scale_color_manual(values = colors)
  } else {
    p <- p + scale_color_viridis_d(option = "H")
  }
  
  return(p)
}
plot_fpc_vecs(vecs = list(fpc[,1],fpc[,2],fpc[,3],fpc[,4]))

```

# optimal cluster number
```{r}
set.seed(123)
optimal_clusters <- function(data, max_clusters = 10, seed = 123) {
  # Load necessary libraries
  require(factoextra)
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # Elbow method: Look at the total within-cluster sum of squares (wss)
  elbow_plot <- fviz_nbclust(data, kmeans, method = "wss", k.max = max_clusters) +
    labs(subtitle = "Elbow Method")
  
  # Silhouette method: Evaluate the average silhouette width for different cluster solutions
  silhouette_plot <- fviz_nbclust(data, kmeans, method = "silhouette", k.max = max_clusters) +
    labs(subtitle = "Silhouette Method")
  
  # Gap Statistic: Compare the change in within-cluster dispersion with that expected under a null reference distribution
  gap_plot <- fviz_nbclust(data, kmeans, nstart = 25, method = "gap_stat", k.max = max_clusters) +
    labs(subtitle = "Gap Statistic")
  
  # Return the three plots as a list
  return(list(elbow = elbow_plot, silhouette = silhouette_plot, gap = gap_plot))
}

# Example usage on your scores_power_sparse data:
results <- optimal_clusters(scores_power_sparse, max_clusters = 10)

# Display the plots:
print(results$elbow)
print(results$silhouette)
print(results$gap)

```

```{r}
plot_expression_color <- function(y,color,title) {
  # Load required libraries
  require(ggplot2)
  require(reshape2)
  require(viridis)
  df <- melt(y)
  names(df) <- c("Series", "Time", "Expression")
  df$Time <- as.numeric(sub("alpha", "", df$Time))
  
  # Create the plot
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Time, y = Expression, group = Series, color = factor(Series))) +
    geom_line(color = color,alpha = 0.4,linewidth = .25) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 119, by = 14),expand = c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-4, 4), breaks = seq(-4, 4, by = 2)) +
    #geom_vline(xintercept = 60, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
    labs(x = "", y = "",title = title) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5))
  return(p)
}

plot_expression_cluster <- function(y, cluster_rows, cp) {
  # Load required libraries
  require(ggplot2)
  require(reshape2)
  
  # Create a vector to hold the cluster assignment for each row of y
  cluster_assignment <- rep(NA, nrow(y))
  for(i in seq_along(cluster_rows)){
    cluster_assignment[cluster_rows[[i]]] <- i
  }
  
  # Force sequential row numbering regardless of row names:
  row_numbers <- seq_len(nrow(y))
  
  # Convert the matrix y into a data frame and add a row identifier column:
  y_df <- as.data.frame(y)
  y_df$row_id <- row_numbers
  
  # Melt the data frame using the row_id as the identifier.
  # This ensures that the "Series" column now corresponds to the row number.
  df <- melt(y_df, id.vars = "row_id")
  names(df) <- c("Series", "Time", "Expression")
  
  # Use the row number (Series) to assign the proper cluster.
  df$cluster <- factor(cluster_assignment[df$Series])
  
  # Process the Time column (remove "alpha" if it is a prefix)
  df$Time <- as.numeric(sub("alpha", "", df$Time))
  
  # Optionally remove rows with NA clusters (if any row did not receive a cluster)
  df <- df[!is.na(df$cluster), ]
  
  # Create the plot with lines colored by their cluster membership
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Time, y = Expression, group = Series, color = cluster)) +
    geom_line(alpha = 0.4,linewidth = .25) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 119, by = 14),expand = c(0,0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-4, 4), breaks = seq(-4, 4, by = 2)) +
    #geom_vline(xintercept = 60, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", size = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cp) +
    labs(x = "", y = "",title = "Raw Data of 542 genes") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "none",plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5))
  
  return(p)
}

```

# Investigating u sparsity on clusters
```{r}
sparse_us <- lapply(seq_len(ncol(res_power_sparse$lsv)),function(i) unname(which(res_power_sparse$lsv[,i] ==0)))

overlap_matrix <- sapply(cluster_rows, function(b) {
  sapply(sparse_us, function(a) {
    length(intersect(a, b))
  })
})
rownames(overlap_matrix) <- paste0("sparse_u", seq_along(sparse_us))
colnames(overlap_matrix) <- paste0("cluster", seq_along(cluster_rows))
sparse_counts <- sapply(sparse_us, length)
cluster_counts <- sapply(cluster_rows, length)
total_overlap <- sum(overlap_matrix)
# Combine the overlap matrix with the sparse_counts as an extra column.
combined_matrix <- rbind(cbind(overlap_matrix, total_sparse = sparse_counts),total_cluster = c(cluster_counts,NA))
combined_matrix

# 
expected_matrix <- outer(sparse_counts, cluster_counts, FUN = function(r, c) (r * c) / total_overlap)
enrichment_matrix <- overlap_matrix / expected_matrix
print(enrichment_matrix)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

# Melt the enrichment matrix for plotting
melted_enrichment <- melt(enrichment_matrix)
names(melted_enrichment) <- c("Sparse", "Cluster", "Enrichment")

# Create a heatmap. Here, a ratio of 1 (white) indicates the expected value,
# red indicates overrepresentation (>1), and blue indicates underrepresentation (<1).
ggplot(melted_enrichment, aes(x = Cluster, y = Sparse, fill = Enrichment)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Enrichment)), color = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Enrichment of sparse_u in Clusters",
       subtitle = "Enrichment Ratio: Observed / Expected",
       x = "Cluster",
       y = "sparse_u")

total_items <- sum(cluster_counts)  # 542 in your case

results <- list()  
results_fisher <- list()

for (i in seq_along(sparse_counts)) {
  results_fisher[[i]] <- list()
  for (j in seq_along(cluster_counts)) {

    A <- overlap_matrix[i, j]
    B <- sparse_counts[i] - A
    C <- cluster_counts[j] - A
    D <- total_items - (A + B + C)
    
    contingency_table <- matrix(c(A, B, C, D), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
    p_value <- fisher.test(contingency_table,alternative = "greater")$p.value
    results_fisher[[i]][[j]] <- fisher.test(contingency_table,alternative = "greater")
    results[[paste0("sparse", i, "_cluster", j)]] <- list(
      table   = contingency_table,
      p_value = p_value
    )
  }
  names(results_fisher[[i]]) <- paste0("cluster",seq_along(cluster_counts))
}
names(results_fisher) <- paste0("sparse",seq_along(sparse_counts))

# Create an empty 4x5 matrix
p_val_matrix <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = 4, ncol = 5)

# Fill it with p-values
for (i in seq_along(sparse_counts)) {
  for (j in seq_along(cluster_counts)) {
    p_val_matrix[i, j] <- results_fisher[[i]][[j]]$p.value
  }
}

# (Optional) add row/col names
rownames(p_val_matrix) <- paste0("sparse", seq_along(sparse_counts))
colnames(p_val_matrix) <- paste0("cluster", seq_along(cluster_counts))
overlap_matrix
combined_matrix
p_val_matrix
```
